findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/verification.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: Test (a) cannot catch the GitHub wait wrongly applied without an origin, because tests use a zero pause.
findings.evidence: Decision 4 sets the pause to zero under cfg(test). With NoCi, fetch returns Ok(None) without calling the runner, so 76 reads at zero pause produce no runner call and no sleep (ci_result.rs:165-170). The claim that '(a) would sleep 75 times' is therefore false; only the direct with_ci_source test (b) checks Wait{polls:1}. Fix: Rewrite the claim to say the no-origin wait is caught by (b), the direct test of with_ci_source checking Wait{polls:1, pause:ZERO}. Keep (b) required. Optionally have (a) record the Wait the closure received through a test hook.

findings.summary: Comparing the exact reuse_statement text against a hand-built CiRecord is brittle, because the statement includes a duration.
findings.evidence: verify.rs:74-77 formats 'Check results for {sha} come from {origin} ({duration_s:.0}s): ...'. The plan builds the expected CiRecord with '..', so the duration must exactly match what parse_ci_run reads from the fake reply. Fix: Build the expected text from the same values the fake replies with (including the duration parse_ci_run would produce), or assert on the parts that matter: the 'Check results for <pushed SHA> come from the CI run <address>' start and each check's 'success'.

findings.summary: The job kind and changed paths decide whether CI is asked and whether checks are skipped, and the harness pins neither.
findings.evidence: routing.rs:100 sets reuse to kind != Build && covers_all. The path rule (skip_when_only) can skip fmt and clippy for prose-only changes in docs/design/study jobs. A skipped check stays skipped on green (routing.rs:210), so its note would not name CI, and a fallback would run fewer than 3 local checks. Fix: State that the CI tests use a reading with class_of_work 'code' (or 'config'), or a candidate that changes a non-prose file, so that no check is skipped and reuse is true. Keep the existing assertion that the runner was called.

findings.summary: If the CI-branch push failed, the checks stage waits the full 1500 s bound before falling back.
findings.evidence: push_ci_branch is called at run/mod.rs:1211, reports a failure only as a warning line and returns nothing. with_ci_source would then poll a branch that does not exist for up to 25 minutes. Fix: Have the producer check whether the push outcome can be passed to with_ci_source from run/mod.rs without editing early.rs. If it can, use NoCi and no wait when the push did not happen. If not, state the limit in the CHANGELOG entry.

findings.summary: The origin rule now exists twice; the pinned test should run against both functions.
findings.evidence: early.rs:305 https_github_repository is private, and the plan adds a copy in client.rs. Fix: Have one test table of the five forms called against both the push-skip path and GhClient::https_repository, so drift between them fails a test.

summary: The plan targets the right place and rests on code that exists. check_and_verify passes routing::NoCi with one read and no wait at run/mod.rs:1278-1289. GhClient::ci_source(branch) at gh/client.rs:706 asks for push runs by head_sha and branch, then reads that run's jobs. read_ci in ci_result.rs:165-189 already treats cancelled and timed-out runs, and runs for another SHA, as missing, so resolve falls back to the local checks. run_routed already turns a red CI run into failed check records. verify::reuse_statement exists, and the plan copies the pattern of extra non-check verifier entries (producer-report-gaps, verification.rs:95). The cfg(test) seam pattern (early_seam) is established, and no athena-cli integration test uses a github.com origin, so building without cfg(test) there is safe. The plan avoids a quiet false pass: the one-check Docs capability would never ask CI (route.reuse needs fmt, clippy and test), so it uses a three-check variant and asserts the fake runner was called. Editing run/verification.rs is needed even though it is not a listed deliverable (Athena already flagged this). Copying the origin rule rather than editing early.rs is a fair trade with a pinned five-form test. Remaining problems are minor: one demonstration's 'fails without' claim is wrong under the zero pause, the exact-text match for the reuse statement is brittle, the CI tests must fix the job kind and changed paths, and a failed CI-branch push costs the full 25-minute wait. No blocker or major findings.
